upon refractive index and the angle of prism.
The advantages of totally reflecting prism over plane mirror are:
i. Comparatively increases the intensity of image.
ii. Does not cause the image laterally inverted.
iii. Comparatively reduces the size of optical instrument.
Importance of Deviation through Small Angled Prism
By controlling and manipulating light precisely while passing through small angled prisms, we can achieve desired optical performance.
A small-angle prism can cause collimation or divergence of light depending on its orientation. This property is used in laser beam expanders, optical metrology systems, etc.

ii. Optical Alignment: The deviation from a small-angled prism can be precisely controlled and measured. This property enables accurate alignment of optical components like lenses, mirrors, filters, etc. for optimal performance of optical systems.
iii. Dispersion Compensation: Small-angled prisms improve performance in fiber optics, spectroscopy and telecommunications by reducing chromatic dispersion.

iv. Image Displacement: Introduction a small angled prism into the optical path allows shifting of the image with minimal degradation. As a result, alignment of optical components, adjustment of path of a beam and redirecting of light in imaging systems become possible.

v. Prism-Based Optical Systems: Small angled prisms serve as fundamental components in optical systems like telescopes, binoculars, and periscopes to create complex functions such as image rotation, light path manipulation, etc.
